subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Gladstone introduced his First Home Rule Bill in which year?
questions.explain: The First Home Rule Bill of 1886 was defeated in the Commons and split the Liberal Party.

questions.q: The Fenian Brotherhood / Irish Republican Brotherhood, founded in 1858, mounted an unsuccessful rising in which year?
questions.explain: The Fenian Rising occurred in 1867; its failure nonetheless kept physical-force republicanism alive.

questions.q: The 15th Amendment, which barred denial of the vote on grounds of race, was ratified in which year?
questions.explain: The 15th Amendment was ratified in 1870, prohibiting voting discrimination based on race.

questions.q: The fall and execution of Robespierre, ending the Terror, occurred in which month and year?
questions.explain: Robespierre was overthrown in the Thermidorian Reaction and guillotined on 28 July 1794 (10 Thermidor Year II).

questions.q: The proposed O'Connell 'monster meeting' that the government banned in 1843 was due to be held at which site?
questions.explain: The Clontarf meeting was banned in October 1843, and O'Connell's decision to call it off marked a decline in the Repeal movement.

questions.q: Gladstone's Second Home Rule Bill of 1893 was passed by the Commons but defeated by which body?
questions.explain: The Second Home Rule Bill passed the Commons in 1893 but was rejected by the House of Lords.

questions.q: In which Supreme Court case did the Court rule school segregation unconstitutional, overturning 'separate but equal'?
questions.explain: Brown v Board of Education declared racial segregation in public schools unconstitutional.

questions.q: In which year was the landmark Brown v Board of Education ruling handed down?
questions.explain: The Supreme Court decided Brown v Board of Education in May 1954.

questions.q: Which constitutional amendment, ratified in 1865, abolished slavery in the United States?
questions.explain: The 13th Amendment, ratified in December 1865, abolished slavery and involuntary servitude.

questions.q: President Lyndon B. Johnson's domestic reform programme of the mid-1960s was known as what?
questions.explain: Johnson's 'Great Society' programme aimed to end poverty and racial injustice, creating Medicare and Medicaid in 1965.

questions.q: The radical phase of the Revolution known as the Terror was dominated by which committee?
questions.explain: The Committee of Public Safety, with Robespierre prominent, directed the Terror of 1793-94 through revolutionary tribunals and emergency powers.

questions.q: The Third Home Rule Bill reached the statute book in 1914 but its operation was suspended because of what?
options: The outbreak of the First World War
questions.explain: The Government of Ireland Act 1914 was placed on the statute book but suspended for the duration of the First World War.

questions.q: The Black Panther Party, advocating self-defence and black empowerment, was founded in 1966 in which city?
questions.explain: Huey Newton and Bobby Seale founded the Black Panther Party in Oakland, California, in 1966.

questions.q: In the 1896 Supreme Court case Plessy v Ferguson, the Court established which doctrine?
questions.explain: Plessy v Ferguson (1896) upheld racial segregation under the 'separate but equal' doctrine.

questions.q: Roughly how many people died during the Great Famine of 1845-49?
questions.explain: Approximately one million people died from starvation and disease during the Famine, with a further million emigrating.

questions.q: The Ulster unionist Solemn League and Covenant against Home Rule was signed in which year?
questions.explain: The Ulster Covenant was signed in September 1912 by hundreds of thousands pledging to resist Home Rule.

questions.q: Which Whig government's Treasury, dominated by laissez-faire principles, oversaw much of the Famine relief from 1846?
questions.explain: Lord John Russell's Whig government took office in 1846 and its laissez-faire approach, associated with Charles Trevelyan, shaped relief policy.

questions.q: The 'Young Ireland' rebellion, a short-lived rising during the Famine years, took place in which year?
questions.explain: The Young Ireland rising of 1848, often called the 'Battle of Widow McCormack's cabbage patch', was a minor affair in County Tipperary.

questions.q: British policy after the Easter Rising, especially the execution of its leaders in May 1916, is generally seen by historians as having what effect?
questions.explain: The execution of sixteen leaders in 1916 generated sympathy and shifted public opinion towards radical separatism and Sinn Fein.

questions.q: The 1917 Italian military catastrophe against Austro-German forces is known as the Battle of which place?
questions.explain: At Caporetto in October-November 1917 the Italian army suffered a devastating defeat, deepening post-war disillusionment.

questions.q: In which year was the Anglo-Irish Treaty signed?
questions.explain: The Anglo-Irish Treaty was signed in London on 6 December 1921.

questions.q: In which year did the assassination of Abraham Lincoln take place, just days after Lee's surrender at Appomattox?
questions.explain: Lincoln was shot by John Wilkes Booth on 14 April 1865 and died the following day, shortly after the Civil War ended.

questions.q: In which year did Napoleon Bonaparte seize power in the coup of 18-19 Brumaire?
questions.explain: Napoleon overthrew the Directory in the coup of Brumaire (9-10 November 1799), establishing the Consulate with himself as First Consul.

questions.q: Which 1920s figure led the 'Back to Africa' movement through the Universal Negro Improvement Association?
questions.explain: Marcus Garvey led the UNIA and promoted black pride and a 'Back to Africa' movement in the 1920s.

questions.q: The Government of Ireland Act 1920 provided for partition by creating how many home-rule parliaments?
questions.explain: The 1920 Act created two parliaments, one for the six counties of Northern Ireland and one for Southern Ireland.

questions.q: On what date did the Parisian crowd storm the Bastille?
questions.explain: The fortress-prison of the Bastille fell to the Parisian crowd on 14 July 1789, a symbolic blow against royal despotism.

questions.q: The Wagner Act of 1935 is significant because it did what?
options: Guaranteed workers' rights to unionise and bargain collectively
questions.explain: The 1935 Wagner (National Labor Relations) Act protected the right of workers to organise and bargain collectively.

questions.q: The Irish War of Independence (Anglo-Irish War) is generally dated from 1919 to which year?
questions.explain: The War of Independence ran from January 1919 until the truce of July 1921.

questions.q: The Irish Civil War over the Treaty was fought principally during which period?
questions.explain: The Civil War ran from June 1922 to May 1923, ending in victory for the pro-Treaty Free State forces.

questions.q: In which year did Parliament pass the Roman Catholic Relief Act granting Catholic Emancipation?
questions.explain: Catholic Emancipation was granted in 1829, allowing Catholics to sit in Parliament.
